messages.subject: Version 1.2.6 released
messages.body_plain:
The version 1.2.6 of the Vim-R-plugin was released:

http://www.vim.org/scripts/script.php?script_id=2628

The changes are:
Improve support for lazy load objects in the Object Browser.
Remove option vimrplugin_vim_window (use $WINDOWID instead).
Fix bug that prevented GVim 64 bit of finding libVimR.dll.
It is necessary to install a new version of the vimcom package:

http://www.lepem.ufc.br/jaa/vimcom.html

messages.subject: Disabling <- shortcut (assignment) and remapping <-
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've come to the vim-r-plugin from years of using Rstudio, and I think it's awesome.

One thing I am used to (for the time being) from using Rstudio is the shortcut alt+- for <-

I also don't like the default binding to _ because I not a fan of using the popular R style of using camelCase or making.variables.like.this in R.  I prefer to define functions and variable names with underscores where needed (r.g. my_variable_name).  The default binding in the vim-r-plugin requires pressing _ twice, which I don't really like as I use underscores so frequently.

1) Is there a straight forward way to disable the shortcut for <-, so that pressing _ always yields the underscore by adjusting the .vimrc file?

I've tried unmap and variations but have not been unsuccessful yet to unmap _.  I am guessing I could hack the vim-r code to change this behaviour, but I have no domain knowledge of this area yet, so I figured I would ask first if there is a simple configuration solution.

2) I have tried to map alt+- to <- like in Rstudio, but so far without success.  I am running Ubuntu.  I can get the alt key mapping to work after various stack overflow searches, but not the dash key.  The best I can do so far is, say, alt+p to get <-  (but it flicks to _ as well on a second press, which isn't a big deal but I don't really like this).  To get the alt+p mapping I added this to .vimrc:

"Get alt key working:
 51 let c='a'
 52 while c <= 'z'
 53     exec "set <A-".c.">=\e".c
 54     exec "imap \e".c." <A-".c.">"
 55     let c = nr2char(1+char2nr(c))
 56 endw
 57
 58 set timeout ttimeoutlen=50
 59
 60 " unmap <_>
 61 imap <A-p> <Esc>:call ReplaceUnderS()<CR>a

Is there by any chance a way to get <alt--> working?  SO suggests shortcuts with alt - may not work, but I figured I'd ask while I'm at it.

Thanks
